attacks.claim: Away Assist can set Away setpoints for occupants who are stationary but home (sleeping, resting, or medically sedentary) because a PIR-style 2 h no-motion rule has no stated exception. The release has no test for a stationary occupant during a scheduled home period.
attacks.evidence: 'sets Away mode after 2 h with no motion during scheduled "home" periods'; QA only lists 'on → Away after 2 h no motion, back on motion' with no stationary-occupant case

attacks.claim: The artifact contradicts its own safety guarantee. Heating is interrupted during each install and during every failed-boot reboot cycle, so 'never interrupted' is false as written.
attacks.evidence: 'freeze/heat protection is never interrupted' vs. 'During the ~90 s install, relays are held open (off)' and 'reverts to 4.7 automatically' after up to 3 failed boots

attacks.claim: Reverting to 4.7 irreversibly deletes users' Home/Away history and silently disables Away Assist, a user setting. The rollback procedure does not mention notifying users or preserving data.
attacks.evidence: 'Away Assist turns off (Home/Away history is deleted)'

attacks.claim: Revert is not bounded in time. It goes through the same OTA path as the install, so it is subject to the 02:00-05:00 window, the HVAC-idle wait, and up to 14-day postponements. Only halting the campaign is immediate. Auto-revert covers only boot failures, not HVAC or behaviour faults on a booting 4.8 unit.
attacks.evidence: 'Revert: push 4.7 to updated units through the same OTA path'; 'Users can postpone an update up to 14 days'; 'Pages ... boot reverts' is the only automatic path; ABSENT: fleet time-to-revert estimate for 612k units

attacks.claim: HVAC coverage is incomplete. The fleet is stratified by HVAC type, but the HIL bench lists only conventional 1H/1C, 2-stage, and heat pump + aux. Boiler, line-voltage, and cooling-only systems are untested, so relay behaviour on those is unverified.
attacks.evidence: 'HIL bench: conventional 1H/1C, 2-stage, heat pump + aux, no C-wire power stealing; rev B/C/D'; 'Each stage is a random sample stratified by hardware rev and HVAC type'; ABSENT: boiler / line-voltage / cooling-only tests

attacks.claim: Power loss or brownout during the flash write or swap is not tested. Installs run overnight with relays off, and the only interruption test is failed-boot injection, which does not cover a partially written slot.
attacks.evidence: 'Failed-boot injection → auto revert to 4.7 | Pass'; ABSENT: power-loss / interrupted-write test during install

attacks.claim: The 8-to-4 period downgrade silently drops user setpoints using a heuristic that is not validated. The QA claim 'correct' is undefined and no case checks which periods are kept, so comfort gaps are possible.
attacks.evidence: 'keeping the 4 periods closest to the user's wake / leave / return / sleep anchors'; 'schedule present and correct'

attacks.claim: The energy claim rests on a 412-home median with no control arm, dispersion, or design described in the artifact. The substantiation is outside the artifact and cannot be checked here, and the claim is published on the listing at launch.
attacks.evidence: 'In our 2025-26 field trial of 412 homes, Away Assist cut heating runtime by a median of 6%'; ABSENT: control design, variance, or trial population detail in the artifact

attacks.claim: Home/Away occupancy inference is a new personal-data category linked to the account, yet the artifact frames it as 'does not change existing data sharing' without stating linkage or any non-app use.
attacks.evidence: 'Only the resulting Home/Away state is sent to the cloud'; 'Away Assist does not change existing data sharing'

attacks.claim: Egress math omits revert and retry traffic. A full revert re-pushes about 1.5 TB more, and 'within the monthly commit' gives no commit figure to check against.
attacks.evidence: 'OTA egress: 2.4 MB image × 612k units ≈ 1.5 TB ... within the monthly commit'

attacks.claim: The +0.4% telemetry projection has no stated events-per-day basis. Motion-driven Home/Away flapping near the 2 h threshold could raise event volume well above that.
attacks.evidence: 'Home/Away state adds ~1 small event per state change; projected +0.4% on telemetry ingest'

attacks.claim: Installs wait until no HVAC call is active with no deadline. In cold-weather households that run heat overnight, updates may never install, and no stall alert exists.
attacks.evidence: 'the unit waits until no HVAC call is active'; ABSENT: install-stall deadline or alert

attacks.claim: Stage-advance gates use HVAC fault telemetry and support contacts, but paging covers only boot reverts and offline rate. 'Not above baseline' is also undefined for small samples such as 6,100 units.
attacks.evidence: 'HVAC fault telemetry not above 4.7 baseline, support contacts per 1k units not above baseline'; 'Pages firmware on-call if boot reverts exceed 0.1% ... or offline rate rises 0.5 points'

attacks.claim: The public timing promise is tighter than the rollout. Stages total 11 days, and postponements can extend delivery beyond 'the next two weeks'.
attacks.evidence: 'Rolling out over the next two weeks'; stage durations 3 + 4 + 4 days plus 'postpone an update up to 14 days'

attacks.claim: The release does not advance the anti-rollback counter, so any previously signed image remains installable. This is acceptable only because the release has no security fixes, and the artifact does not record that as a standing decision.
attacks.evidence: 'does not increment the secure-boot anti-rollback counter (no security fixes in this release), so 4.7 remains installable'

attacks.claim: Signed images and bootloader verification are described, but the authorization model for the new Home/Away cloud store and its ingest endpoint is not described.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: authn/authz for the Home/Away state endpoint. Only 'Images are signed (Ed25519)' is stated.

attacks.claim: Occupancy (Home/Away) data is newly stored in the cloud for 7 days. The artifact asserts it is not exposed to partners, but gives no access-control evidence, and it does not address whether a privacy impact assessment was done (e.g. Quebec).
attacks.evidence: 'Home/Away state is not exposed through the partner integrations API.' ABSENT: test or access-control evidence for this claim.

attacks.claim: Occupancy data now lives in the vendor cloud with no stated self-host or local-only option for Away Assist; exit path for this data is not described.
attacks.evidence: 'Only the resulting Home/Away state is sent to the cloud (needed to show it in the app); it is kept 7 days and then deleted.'

attacks.claim: Motion-driven Home/Away flips (pets, brief motion) are not debounced, so event volume could exceed the +0.4% projection, which assumes no adoption rate.
attacks.evidence: 'returns to schedule on the first motion' / 'Home/Away state adds ~1 small event per state change; projected +0.4%'

attacks.claim: Egress is computed, but the 'monthly commit' is not quantified, and retries, postponements and revert pushes are not counted.
attacks.evidence: 'within the monthly commit' with no commit figure. 'projected +0.4% on telemetry ingest' with no baseline or adoption assumption.

attacks.claim: Power loss during the ~90 s install, with relays held off, is not covered by any QA test. Failed-boot injection does not establish safe recovery from a cut during flash write, and HVAC is off in the meantime.
attacks.evidence: 'During the ~90 s install, relays are held open (off).' QA table lists only 'Failed-boot injection → auto revert to 4.7'. ABSENT: power-cut-during-install test.

attacks.claim: Alerting pages only on boot reverts and offline rate. Fault-code and HVAC telemetry regressions gate stage advance but do not page, and nothing halts automatically.
attacks.evidence: 'Pages firmware on-call if boot reverts exceed 0.1%… or offline rate rises 0.5 points.' 'Halt: pause the OTA campaign (one switch)'.

attacks.claim: Rollback latency is not bounded. Revert uses the same OTA path, which is subject to the 02:00-05:00 install window and the temperature deferral, so a defective 4.8 may keep running for a long time. Revert timing is not stated.
attacks.evidence: 'Revert: push 4.7 to updated units through the same OTA path.' ABSENT: time-to-revert and whether install window and temperature deferral apply to revert.

attacks.claim: A 4.7 schedule edit silently and permanently discards the stored v2 schedule, so periods beyond the first four are lost for good on re-upgrade. The user is not told at the point of loss.
attacks.evidence: 'the cloud discards the stale v2 copy, so a later re-upgrade starts from the current v1 schedule.' The only user message is 'Some schedule changes were simplified'.

attacks.claim: Away Assist can drop setpoints to Away while occupants are asleep or still. Sleep is a scheduled home period, and a motionless sleeper for 2 h would trigger Away. The QA test only covers a generic no-motion case.
attacks.evidence: 'sets Away mode after 2 h with no motion during scheduled "home" periods'. QA: 'on → Away after 2 h no motion, back on motion'. ABSENT: test for motionless sleeping occupant or sensor coverage.

attacks.claim: Returning to schedule on first motion may land the unit in a scheduled Away period, and the artifact does not state the resulting setpoint.
attacks.evidence: 'returns to schedule on the first motion'

attacks.claim: Some claimed behaviours have no QA evidence: the stale-v2 re-upgrade path, Away Assist state after revert, and app 9.3 edits made while a unit is on 4.7.
attacks.evidence: 'a later re-upgrade starts from the current v1 schedule' and 'Away Assist turns off (Home/Away history is deleted)' are not in the QA table.

attacks.claim: HIL coverage excludes power-stealing installs, which are common in retrofits. The 72 h bench run is short against a random fleet sample.
attacks.evidence: 'conventional 1H/1C, 2-stage, heat pump + aux, no C-wire power stealing' / '0 relay faults over 72 h'

attacks.claim: Deferral rules are stated in Celsius only. The artifact does not say whether the device or app shows the deferral reason in the user's units.
attacks.evidence: 'Install is deferred if indoor temperature is below 7 °C or above 32 °C'

attacks.claim: The energy benefit is a median from one trial and applies only to users who opt in, while the release leads with the feature.
attacks.evidence: 'cut heating runtime by a median of 6%' / 'Away Assist is off for every user until they turn it on.'

attacks.claim: The install waits until no HVAC call is active with no stated maximum wait, and users can postpone 14 days. The end-of-postpone behaviour is not described.
attacks.evidence: 'the unit waits until no HVAC call is active' / 'Users can postpone an update up to 14 days from the app.'

attacks.claim: App screens were tested with VoiceOver, TalkBack and 200% text. The thermostat's own display and Away Assist indicators have no stated accessibility check.
attacks.evidence: 'App 9.3 schedule editor and Away Assist screens with VoiceOver, TalkBack, 200% text' / device display not mentioned.

attacks.claim: Changed control logic and relay sequencing may need safety re-evaluation or certification, and no statement covers it. Canadian privacy-law PIA obligations for new personal-data flows are also unaddressed.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: safety certification review for changed control logic. Only 'legal review LGL-4471' and 'LGL-4472' are cited.

attacks.claim: Dual-writing v1 and v2 schedules on every edit creates a long-lived compatibility obligation: 4.7 must read v1 indefinitely and the cloud must sync both.
attacks.evidence: 'it also writes a v1 schedule (4 periods) on every edit… the cloud stores both'

attacks.claim: The release notes promise completion in two weeks, but staged gating with advance criteria can extend past that.
attacks.evidence: 'Rolling out over the next two weeks.' against stage durations of 3, 4, 4 days plus gates.

attacks.claim: The agreed invariant is that devices can always return to the previous firmware, but the only revert path is an OTA push of 4.7, which requires a 4.8 unit to stay reachable. 4.8 changes Wi-Fi reconnect behaviour, and auto-revert triggers only on boot or self-test failure. A 4.8 unit that boots but cannot reconnect is stranded, and no local rollback is described.
attacks.evidence: Revert: push 4.7 to updated units through the same OTA path ... If 4.8 fails to boot or fails its post-boot self-test 3 times, the unit reverts to 4.7 automatically

attacks.claim: The freeze-protection claim is contradicted elsewhere in the artifact. Relays are held open during install, and boot-revert loops repeat that outage. Indoor 7 °C is also a weak freeze threshold for unheated spaces and pipe runs.
attacks.evidence: so freeze/heat protection is never interrupted ... During the ~90 s install, relays are held open (off)

attacks.claim: Away Assist sets Away after 2 h with no motion during home periods. A sedentary or sleeping occupant, such as an elderly or medically vulnerable person, or a sensor false negative can trigger setback. No occupant-safety override or false-Away test is described.
attacks.evidence: sets Away mode after 2 h with no motion during scheduled 'home' periods; ABSENT: occupant-safety override and sensor false-negative test

attacks.claim: No precedence rule is defined when v1 and v2 schedules disagree. For example, an app 9.2 edit to v1 on a unit with a stored v2 could leave 4.8 running a stale 8-period schedule and ignoring the user's change.
attacks.evidence: the cloud discards the stale v2 copy (only stated for 4.7 edits); ABSENT: rule for writes from app 9.2 or other paths

attacks.claim: Home/Away events are also sent to telemetry ingest, which has no stated retention or deletion path. The 7-day deletion promise may therefore not cover all stored occupancy data.
attacks.evidence: it is kept 7 days and then deleted ... Home/Away state adds ~1 small event per state change; projected +0.4% on telemetry ingest

attacks.claim: Rollback silently deletes Home/Away history, disables Away Assist, and collapses schedules to v1. The artifact defines no user notice or consent step for these losses, and the release notes do not mention them.
attacks.evidence: Away Assist turns off (Home/Away history is deleted); schedules fall back to their v1 copy

attacks.claim: HVAC fault codes are dashboard-only with no paging. Stage 1 (~6,100 units for 3 days) is too small to detect low-rate relay faults, and the advance thresholds have no stated statistical basis.
attacks.evidence: Pages firmware on-call if boot reverts exceed 0.1% ... or offline rate rises 0.5 points; HVAC fault codes listed only in the dashboard

attacks.claim: The claim that no raw motion data leaves the device and that Home/Away is not exposed to partners has no supporting test in the QA table.
attacks.evidence: No raw motion data leaves the thermostat ... ABSENT: test evidence for this claim

attacks.claim: QA gaps: 'correct' schedule is undefined, the 4-period v1 selection rule is unspecified, the revert path with Away Assist enabled is not in the QA table, and motion-sensor presence on rev B/C/D is not stated.
attacks.evidence: 'schedule present and correct'; 'keeping the 4 periods closest to the user's wake / leave / return / sleep anchors'

attacks.claim: Signing-key custody and rotation are not described, and device-to-cloud authentication for the new Home/Away state is not described.
attacks.evidence: Images are signed (Ed25519); ABSENT: key management and auth for the Home/Away endpoint

attacks.claim: OTA delivery depends on a single existing CDN contract, with no described fallback or exit path for a 1.5 TB fleet push.
attacks.evidence: via existing CDN contract

attacks.claim: All 612k units share the same 02:00-05:00 local window across US and Canadian time zones with no stated download jitter. Each edit also doubles schedule writes.
attacks.evidence: Install window 02:00-05:00 local; 4.8 ... writes a v1 schedule (4 periods) on every edit

attacks.claim: The egress estimate excludes retries, halt/resume, and revert re-downloads, which could roughly double the transfer. The +0.4% telemetry figure is an unsourced projection.
attacks.evidence: OTA egress: 2.4 MB image × 612k units ≈ 1.5 TB ... projected +0.4% on telemetry ingest

attacks.claim: The public energy claim rests on a single 412-home trial, and the artifact gives no dispersion, control design, or stratification by rev or HVAC type. The substantiation sits behind an external link.
attacks.evidence: cut heating runtime by a median of 6% ... Methodology and trial data are linked at hearthline.com/away-assist-trial

attacks.claim: Storing and writing both v1 and v2 schedules indefinitely adds ongoing dual-format complexity with no retirement plan.
attacks.evidence: 4.8 stores schedules as v2 (8 periods). It also writes a v1 schedule (4 periods) on every edit

attacks.claim: Behaviour after the 14-day postponement expires is unstated, and a cold snap that keeps indoor temperature below 7 °C could defer install indefinitely with no escalation.
attacks.evidence: Users can postpone an update up to 14 days ... Install is deferred if indoor temperature is below 7 °C

attacks.claim: No gate-worthy issue under this lens.
attacks.evidence: n/a
